 Order

The petitioner is before this Court calling in question order dated 31-12-2013 by which the properties in plot No.1 measuring 20 acres and plot No.2 part of IT park measuring 11.50 acres which were proposed to be allotted to the petitioner in which respondent No.2/Karnataka Industrial Area Development Board ('the Board' for short) had formed IT Zone, Devanahalli, is cancelled.

2. Heard Sri D.R. Ravishankar, learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner, Smt. Shwetha Krishnappa, learned Additional Government Advocate appearing for the respondent No.1 and Sri B.B. Patil, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2.
3.
Brief facts that lead the petitioner to this court in the subject petition, as borne out from the pleadings are as follows:-
The lands owned by the petitioner were notified for acquisition by issuance of a preliminary notification on 09-01-2007 and later a final notification on 15-05-2007.
The petitioner aggrieved by the said notification knocked at the doors of this Court in Writ Petition No.16367 of 2007.
This Court disposed of the writ petition on a memo filed by the Board by its order dated 06-08- 2010.

It appears that during the M/S Ranka And Shah Developers Pvt Ltd vs State Of Karnataka on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87654378/
2 pendency of the petition, in a proceeding before the 17th High Level Clearance Committee held on 28-01-2009, the subject of such acquisition was placed and the Committee resolved to consider allotting the land to the petitioner in lieu of lands acquired.

sentences.text: In terms of the resolution, an order was passed on 07-12-2009 giving details about the infrastructure to be provided in the lands that were to be allotted in favour of the petitioner and the like.
Based on the said order a letter was issued to the petitioner on 24-07-2010 and this letter was annexed to the memo that was placed before this Court in Writ Petition No.16367 of 2007.

4. The petitioner later represents to the Board on 22-11-2010 seeking allotment of 33 acres and 31 guntas of land in lieu of surrendered land in the proposed IT/ITES park being set up out of the lands acquired in that region in terms of what was allotted by this Court while disposing of Writ Petition No.16367 of 2007.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer takes over the lands of the petitioner not to the whole extent but to an extent of 29 acres 1 gunta.
The petitioner was seeking a particular plot to be in lieu of acquisition of its land.
One more representation was given on 05-09-2012 which resulted in the impugned communication dated 31-12-2013 directing the petitioner to pay development costs of the land at `15,75,75,000/-.
Since this was in lieu of acquisition, the development costs were alone to be paid in terms of the Rules and Regulations of the Board.
The petitioner again makes a representation on 27-07-2016 three years after passing of the order requesting reconsideration of development charges.
The petitioner not paying development costs goes on making representations to the Board seeking issuance of allotment letter by reconsideration of development charges.
5. The representations were made on 27-02-2018 and 05-07- 2018.

A representation was also made on 03-03-2022 to which the Board replies stating that unless development costs are paid, the land cannot be allotted and the petitioner but was free to claim compensation as is paid to other land owners who have not sought allotment of any plot in lieu of acquisition.
It is at that juncture, the petitioner has knocked at the doors of this Court in the subject petition.
This Court entertaining the petition had directed that the subject plots should not be allotted or encumbered if that had not happened yet.
The same is continuing even as on this day.

6. The learned senior counsel representing the petitioner would contend with vehemence that the land of the petitioner is taken away and what is to be allotted becomes its property under Article 300 of the Constitution of India and therefore, claiming development charges upon that is unavailable to the Board.
Under the very Act, the petitioner is entitled to hold the land in lieu of compensation in terms of the resolution of the Board and the Government orders issued in the year 2009.
He would contend that payment of development charges has no basis for the lands that are acquired in the teeth of no compensation being paid to the land owner, the petitioner.
7. On the other hand, the learned counsel Sri B.B. Patil representing the 2nd respondent would vehemently refute the submission to contend that the land that is allotted is in lieu of compensation.
The petitioner cannot claim that development charges also cannot be laid upon the land owner whose land is acquired and allotment is made in lieu of compensation.
He would submit that since 2013 the petitioner has gone on dodging the issue of payment of development charges.

It has neither M/S Ranka And Shah Developers Pvt Ltd vs State Of Karnataka on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87654378/
3 permitted the land to be developed nor the land to be granted to others.

sentences.text: It is always open to the petitioner to seek compensation for the land that it has lost as allotment of land today is 10 years old and the petitioner is in default of payment of development charges.
Not a rupee of development charges is paid for the last 10 years.
8. I have given my anxious consideration to the submissions made by the respective learned counsel and have perused the material on record.
9. The petitioner did own certain extent of land as is observed hereinabove.
Those lands became subject matter of acquisition.
The acquisition was challenged before this Court in Writ Petition No.16367 of 2007.

During the pendency of the writ petition, the petitioner was given clearance by the State High Level Clearance Committee in its meeting held on 28-01-2009 to establish IT/ITES SEZ at Board's layout for IT Sector at Devanahalli which was a part of investment of `430 crores

The resolution of the Board reads as follows:
"The Committee resolved to permit the company to establish the unit in 33 acres 31 guntas of land to be allotted by KIADB in the layout for IT sector at Devanahalli in lieu of the land he shall surrender to KIADB.
The project proponent shall pay development charges to KIADB for the same."

The resolution of the Committee was to permit the company i.e., the petitioner to establish the unit in 33 acres and 31 guntas of land to be allotted by the Board in lieu of land that it has surrendered to the Board.
The project proponent, the petitioner was to pay development charges to the Board for the same.

This resolution was placed before the Court in Writ Petition No.16367 of 2007 and this Court recording the memo disposed of the petition by the following order:
"Taking on record the memo dated 28-07-2010 enclosing the copy of the letter dated 24-07-2010 addressed to the petitioner informing the petitioner that the AKIADB in its meeting held on 5-09-2010 approved a plan for industrial area and the development works in the said area are under progress, the allotment letter indicating plot number and terms and conditions of allotment including developmental charges payable by the petitioner will be issued in due course, nothing further survives for consideration in this petition and is, accordingly, disposed of.

It is needless to state that if the petitioner is not allotted the site within six months from to-day, provided the petitioner ensures that the property, subject matter of acquisition is free from all admitted litigation, is entitled to re-open the case."
(Emphasis supplied)

The Court recorded the memo which enclosed the resolution supra and observed that the allotment letter indicating plot number and terms of allotment including development charges payable by the petitioner would be issued in due course and therefore, nothing survives for consideration in the petition and the allotment was directed to be made within six months from the said date.

Based on the above communication we surrendered all the documents of our land to the SLAO of M/s KIADB on 8.06.2011 (vide our letter dated 4-06-2011) duly acknowledged.

W e w e r e s u r p r i s e d t o r e c e i v e a l e t t e r f r o m t h e J o i n t D i r e c t o r o f M / s K I A D B No.IADB/HO/Allot/JD/18635 /2013-14 dated 31-12-2013, rightly citing the above referred 17th SHLCC meeting of 28-01-2009 as having approved and cleared allotment of 33 acres 31 guntas of land, but, wrongly citing the above 8-06-20l1 order of the Honourable High Court of Karnataka as having ordered for ".... Considering allotment of land after collecting necessary development cost."
And further asking us to pay `15,75,75,000/- to enable further action in the matter by M/s KIADB.

Though the letter confirmed our having handed over the lands and original documents to M/s KIADB it was not an Allotment letter as per M/s KIADB's above letter dated 24-07-2010, and,
averments and submissions while filing the same letter vide Memo dated 28-07-2010 as filed by M/s KIADB before the Honorable Karnataka High Court the High Court which accordingly disposed of the petition [WP No.16367 of 2009 (LA-KIADB)] vide its 06-08-2020 order - all of which are clear that that the Allotment letter will be issued along with terms and conditions of allotment and payable development charge.

We have continuously been following up as you are bound to issue the Allotment Letter with all the terms and conditions as we have already complied with the terms for obtaining the allotment i.e., surrender of our land to the KIADB and withdrawal of case.
We received a communication from AIADB on 3.10.2018 to get extension of the time project from SHLCC.
This we are required to do only if we have not taken up the project within the stipulated time of 3-5 years of our having received the Allotment Letter from yourself.

The petitioner even after 12 years of disposal of Writ Petition No.16367 of 2009 clings upon the said order and submits that the development charges that are asked for were contrary to the order and therefore, it cannot form a part of allotment letter.
This representation comes about 12 years after the disposal of the petition and close to 9 years after the impugned communication.

This is replied to by the Board on 26-04-2022 observing that unless development charges were paid no allotment in favour of the petitioner could be made as the Court did not observe that development charges need not be paid.

sentences.text: As a matter of fact the order of the Court was recording the memo which reads that the allotment would be made in terms of certain terms and conditions that would be drawn for such allotment and includes development charges payable by the petitioner.
Recording this memo, the Court had disposed of the petition.
Therefore, if the petitioner wanted allotment or lease-cum- sale agreement to be executed, it ought to have complied with the communication for payment of development charges.
It was directed to be paid within 30 days from the communication dated 31-12-2013.
30 days time is long over - not only 30 days, 30 months or even three years are over.
The communication is now 10 years old.
Even today the petitioner has not paid development charges as was demanded.
11. The submission made that it is the property of the petitioner who has a right over it under Article 300 of the Constitution of India and that cannot be taken away is unacceptable.
The land was always available to the petitioner subject to certain conditions of development.

The learned counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent/Board would submit that the petitioner has defaulted in payment of development charges and, therefore, the allotment of plot cannot be made in its favour and it is always open to the petitioner to claim compensation in accordance with law for acquisition of its property.

This submission merits acceptance in the peculiar facts of this case, as the petitioner for nearly 10 years did not come forward to pay a single rupee towards development charges out of `15,75,75,000/- that was demanded.

Therefore, finding no merit in the petition to set aside the order dated 31-12-2013 after 10 years of its issuance, I deem it appropriate to preserve the right of the petitioner to receive payment of compensation for its lands that have been acquired.
The payment of compensation shall be assessed in accordance with law and disbursed to the petitioner without brooking any delay.

12. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER (i) Writ Petition stands disposed.
(ii) The challenge to the impugned order dated 31-12-2013 stands rejected.
(iii) The petitioner is held entitled to payment of compensation for its lands that have been acquired, along with interest and all other benefits, in accordance with law.
(iv) The compensation shall be paid to the petitioner within four weeks from the date of receipt of the copy of this order, if not earlier.
Consequently, pending applications also stand disposed.

The lands owned by the petitioner were notified for acquisition by issuance of a preliminary notification on 09-01-2007 and later a final notification on 15-05-2007.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer takes over the lands of the petitioner not to the whole extent but to an extent of 29 acres 1 gunta.
The petitioner was seeking a particular plot to be in lieu of acquisition of its land.
The resolution of the Committee was to permit the company i.e., the petitioner to establish the unit in 33 acres and 31 guntas of land to be allotted by the Board in lieu of land that it has surrendered to the Board.
The said decision was filed in the "High Court" & the Court disposed of the petition in 2010 directing M/s. KIADB to allot land in 6 months.
The development charges levied should only be as per the rates in 2010 (when the Honorable high Court) passed the order & not as on 31-03-2013.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Under the very Act, the petitioner is entitled to hold the land in lieu of compensation in terms of the resolution of the Board and the Government orders issued in the year 2009.
He would contend that payment of development charges has no basis for the lands that are acquired in the teeth of no compensation being paid to the land owner, the petitioner.
The petitioner cannot claim that development charges also cannot be laid upon the land owner whose land is acquired and allotment is made in lieu of compensation.
It is always open to the petitioner to seek compensation for the land that it has lost as allotment of land today is 10 years old and the petitioner is in default of payment of development charges.
Not a rupee of development charges is paid for the last 10 years.

Therefore, finding no merit in the petition to set aside the order dated 31-12-2013 after 10 years of its issuance, I deem it appropriate to preserve the right of the petitioner to receive payment of compensation for its lands that have been acquired.
The payment of compensation shall be assessed in accordance with law and disbursed to the petitioner without brooking any delay.
12. For the aforesaid reasons, the following:
ORDER (i) Writ Petition stands disposed.
(ii) The challenge to the impugned order dated 31-12-2013 stands rejected.
(iii) The petitioner is held entitled to payment of compensation for its lands that have been acquired, along with interest and all other benefits, in accordance with law.
(iv) The compensation shall be paid to the petitioner within four weeks from the date of receipt of the copy of this order, if not earlier.
Consequently, pending applications also stand disposed.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Court recorded the memo which enclosed the resolution supra and observed that the allotment letter indicating plot number and terms of allotment including development charges payable by the petitioner would be issued in due course and therefore, nothing survives for consideration in the petition and the allotment was directed to be made within six months from the said date.
Though the letter confirmed our having handed over the lands and original documents to M/s KIADB it was not an Allotment letter as per M/s KIADB's above letter dated 24-07-2010, and,
averments and submissions while filing the same letter vide Memo dated 28-07-2010 as filed by M/s KIADB before the Honorable Karnataka High Court the High Court which accordingly disposed of the petition [WP No.16367 of 2009 (LA-KIADB)] vide its 06-08-2020 order - all of which are clear that that the Allotment letter will be issued along with terms and conditions of allotment and payable development charge.
The petitioner even after 12 years of disposal of Writ Petition No.16367 of 2009 clings upon the said order and submits that the development charges that are asked for were contrary to the order and therefore, it cannot form a part of allotment letter.

30 days time is long over - not only 30 days, 30 months or even three years are over.
The land was always available to the petitioner subject to certain conditions of development.
